questions.stem: At what local times is the Pacific regular marine forecast issued?
questions.explanation: The regular forecast and technical synopsis are issued four times a day at those times.

questions.stem: At what times are the extended and wave height forecasts issued?
What does the extended forecast give?
options: Wind, waves and fog for days 1 to 2
Wave height only, for days 3 to 5
Tides and currents for the week
questions.explanation: The regular forecast covers days 1 and 2; the extended gives wind for days 3 to 5.

questions.stem: What is the correct order of items in a regular forecast?
options: Wind, warnings, area name, fog, then temperature
Title, fog, area, warnings, then wind, weather, spray and temperature
Air temperature, wind, warnings, title, then the area name
Warnings, wind, area name, then the fog statement and visibility
questions.explanation: That is the guide's order, each element only when it applies.

questions.stem: What does 'fog' mean in an Environment Canada marine forecast?
questions.explanation: The fixed line says fog implies visibility less than 1 mile.

questions.stem: A forecast says 'tonight'. Which period does that cover?
questions.explanation: Tonight is 6:00 p.m. to 5:59 a.m. (or from issue time if issued after 6 p.m.).

questions.stem: In a forecast, wind is stated once as 'northwest 15 knots' and no later line changes it. What does that mean?
options: It will drop to calm later
It will double later in the day
It is expected to persist through the rest of the period
The forecast is incomplete for that period and should be ignored

questions.stem: What does a wave height forecast give for 'significant wave height'?
options: The height of the largest single wave
The mean of the highest third of waves, in metres
The height of the swell only, in metres, from distant storms
The average of all the waves, in feet
questions.explanation: ECCC defines it this way; seas are in metres.

questions.stem: On the BC coast the Coast Guard continuous marine broadcast is on:
questions.explanation: RAMN Part 2 shows Channel 21B; UBC describes the loop and the update times.

questions.stem: From which transmitters does Prince Rupert MCTS send NAVTEX (518 kHz)?
options: Texada Island and Port Hardy light stations

questions.stem: Which of these is a 'significant change' in wind in the guide?
options: A change of 1 knot or more
A change of 3 knots or more in speed
A change of 10 knots or more
Any change in wind at all
questions.explanation: Also a direction change of more than 45 degrees (when the compared speed exceeds 10 knots) or a change in warning category.

questions.stem: In the invented forecast 'Wind southeast 25 to 35 knots becoming northwest 15 to 25 late this evening', when does the shift occur?
questions.explanation: Late evening is 9:00 to 11:59 p.m., so the shift is expected then.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a Pacific marine forecast area name?
questions.explanation: The listed areas include Haro Strait, Johnstone Strait and Queen Charlotte Strait; Burrard Inlet North is not a forecast area name in the RAMN list.
